abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel paradigm shift in software quality modeling by introducing a holistic quantum-inspired framework that transcends traditional static quality assessment approaches. Conventional quality models predominantly rely on deterministic metrics that fail to capture the inherently uncertain and dynamic nature of software evolution. Our research proposes the Quantum Uncertainty Quality Model (QUQM), which conceptualizes software quality attributes as probabilistic wave functions that evolve through development phases. The framework employs superposition principles to represent multiple possible quality states simultaneously, enabling more accurate prediction of software reliability under varying operational conditions. We formalize the mathematical foundations of QUQM using density matrix representations and demonstrate its theoretical advantages through rigorous proofs of convergence. Empirical validation using 847 software projects from diverse domains confirms that QUQM achieves 34% improvement in reliability prediction accuracy compared to Bayesian network approaches. The proposed paradigm fundamentally reconceptualizes how practitioners should approach software quality assessment, shifting from point-estimate metrics toward probability distribution-based quality characterization. This work contributes a foundational theoretical apparatus that opens new research directions in uncertainty-aware software engineering.

Software maintainability prediction remains a critical challenge in quality assurance, yet existing prediction models suffer from significant limitations in handling class imbalance and temporal concept drift. This paper advances the state of the art by developing an enhanced theoretical framework that integrates concept drift detection with ensemble learning for maintainability prediction. We first establish a formal taxonomy of drift patterns specific to maintainability metrics, categorizing them into abrupt, gradual, and recurrent types. Building upon this taxonomy, we propose the Adaptive Maintainability Prediction Framework (AMPF) that dynamically weights ensemble components based on detected drift characteristics. The theoretical analysis proves that AMPF achieves lower prediction variance under concept drift conditions compared to single-model approaches. We derive closed-form expressions for optimal ensemble weights as functions of drift magnitude and feature relevance stability. Extensive experiments conducted on 12 open-source systems spanning eight years of development history demonstrate that AMPF reduces prediction error by 23% on average while maintaining consistent performance across different drift types. This framework significantly improves practical applicability of maintainability prediction in long-lived software systems.

This paper introduces SAQuA (Security-Aware Quality Assurance Architecture), a novel architectural paradigm that fundamentally reconceptualizes the integration of security quality within software quality management systems. Existing approaches treat security as a separate concern that must be grafted onto quality assurance processes, resulting in fragmented assessments and missed vulnerabilities. SAQuA proposes an ontological architecture where security properties are intrinsically woven into the fabric of quality models from inception. The system implements a multi-layered quality assessment engine comprising static analysis modules, dynamic behavior monitoring components, and predictive threat modeling capabilities that operate as unified processes rather than isolated tools. Key innovations include the Security-Quality Dependency Graph (SQDG) for modeling complex interdependencies and the Real-time Quality-Security Fusion Engine (QSFE) that performs simultaneous assessment. We detail the architectural components, communication protocols, and extension mechanisms that enable integration with existing development environments. Evaluation using a comprehensive benchmark suite demonstrates that SAQuA identifies 47% more security-related quality issues while reducing assessment time by 62% compared to traditional toolchains. This architectural paradigm shift enables fundamentally more effective security quality management.

Automated software testing remains resource-intensive despite advances in test generation techniques, with practitioners struggling to balance coverage adequacy with testing cost constraints. This paper presents TestOptima, an enhanced testing optimization system that significantly improves upon existing approaches through intelligent test suite optimization. The system implements a multi-objective optimization engine that simultaneously maximizes fault detection effectiveness while minimizing execution cost and maintenance burden. TestOptima introduces several architectural improvements over prior systems: a graph-based test dependency analyzer that identifies redundancies with greater precision, a machine learning-based prioritization module that predicts test effectiveness with improved accuracy, and an adaptive allocation algorithm that dynamically distributes testing resources based on risk assessment. The system's core innovation lies in its hybrid optimization strategy that combines genetic algorithms with constraint programming, achieving superior convergence properties. We describe the complete system architecture, implementation details, and APIs that facilitate integration with CI/CD pipelines. Controlled experiments on 15 industrial software systems reveal that TestOptima achieves 28% higher fault detection rates while reducing testing time by 41% compared to state-of-the-art approaches. The system demonstrates practical viability through successful deployment in three production environments.
